metadata.title: Powder River Basin Geological Context: Remington Study Area
metadata.description: Stratigraphic and historical combustion framework for interpreting coal seam fire evidence.
sources: Montana Bureau of Mines and Geology (MBMG) Coal Program

properties.name: Tongue River Member (Fort Union Formation)
properties.description: Primary thick coal-bearing stratigraphic interval of northern Powder River Basin. Contains Wyodak-Anderson, Canyon, Dietz, and Roland coal beds.
properties.combustionSusceptibility: High at shallow weathered outcrop and subcrop zones; susceptible to spontaneous combustion upon exposure to atmospheric oxygen and thermal trigger.
properties.provenance: USGS Professional Paper 1809 / MBMG Report of Investigation 25

properties.name: Tongue River - Powder River Divide Clinker Belt
properties.description: Resistant red/orange baked shale and paralava formed by prehistoric and historical in-situ burning of the Anderson and Wyodak coal beds.
properties.significance: Establishes long-term geologic precedent of self-sustaining coal seam combustion in this specific terrain, independent of recent fire events.
properties.provenance: USGS NCRA Professional Paper 1625-A Digital GIS Layers (prbclkg)

properties.name: Wasatch Formation (Overburden / Basin Center)
properties.description: Interbedded sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone conformably overlying Fort Union coals in elevated tablelands.
properties.combustionSusceptibility: Low (acts as thermal insulating cap and overburden; combustion occurs where eroded by dendritic drainage).
